evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check only requires positive and different manager PIDs and nonempty, different invocation IDs. A guest reboot between the two manager snapshots can change both values, so the check can accept a manager restart that was actually caused by a guest reboot rather than the intended isolated restart. The report already has boot IDs in the snapshot shape for the reboot check, so requiring nonempty equal boot IDs in the manager before/after pair is a small correctness fix, not a new protection scope.
